images.title: Under the Door
images.prompt: Painterly cinematic still, an old 1920s river hotel at night, 1970s paranoid-thriller restraint, opaque gouache brush drag, practical lamps only, bottle-green cloth wallpaper, worn varnish, thumb-polished brass, tobacco-amber lamplight against river-grey light, brown-black shadow, soft film grain. Five in the morning in a very long, very narrow hidden service passage, camera centred looking straight down its length, symmetrical one-point perspective, no people. Along the left wall a row of six narrow dark varnished doors, each with a small round brass peephole rose that is dark and unlit, no light behind any of them. The bottle-green walls and the ceiling are completely bare and dark: no frames, no pictures, no wall lamps, no ceiling lamps. A small postcard-sized sheet of blue-black carbon paper lies half slid under the nearest door, its corner showing on the dark floorboards, a thin dark sliver rather than a mat. Dead centre at the far end, a seventh plain door whose peephole alone glows: one tiny bright amber point, the only warm light in the picture. Thin river-grey dawn from high windows on the right, threadbare runner, dark wainscot. Emptied, waiting. The lower quarter is quiet dark floorboards. No text, no lettering, no watermark, no logo.
images.needs_review: Retry 2 kept (frames, wall and ceiling lamps gone, only the far peephole lit). Still off: the carbon sheet sits at the bottom-left corner of the frame with faint pseudo-print on it, not clearly sliding under the nearest door.

images.title: The Wrong Picture

Dawn in a double-height marble hotel lobby, a high wide view looking down from the mezzanine, all figures tiny and far below. Three small figures walk away from us in a row toward the revolving door: a hotel guest in a plain overcoat carrying one small suitcase, flanked by two uniformed police officers seen from behind, one on each side, unhurried, nobody touching anybody; the guest looks back over one shoulder and up toward the camera, face too small and shadowed to read. Apart from them, alone at the reception desk on the right, a night clerk in a waistcoat faces the camera and raises a black telephone receiver high above his head toward the mezzanine, offering it to the viewer. Flat river-grey daylight through the revolving door, a brass chandelier still burning amber. The lower quarter is the calm dark varnished mezzanine rail and shadow. images.title: The Sitter
images.prompt: Painterly cinematic still, an old 1920s river hotel at night, 1970s paranoid-thriller restraint, opaque gouache brush drag, practical lamps only, bottle-green cloth wallpaper, worn varnish, thumb-polished brass, tobacco-amber lamplight against river-grey light, brown-black shadow, soft film grain. Close view of a small watercolour on cream paper, pinned with one brass pin to bottle-green cloth wallpaper, no people. The watercolour shows a plain varnished door at the end of a narrow passage; the door's peephole is painted as a single warm glowing amber dot, the brightest point in the frame, with no separate dark rose or ring beside it. In the paper's bottom corner a tiny filled circle of brass-gold paint, not red. Loose washes of river grey and amber, pencil lines showing, one corner of the sheet curling. On a desk edge below, out of focus, a folded pair of white cotton gloves. Soft dim even light, no lamp or bulb visible in frame, no glare, a soft shadow behind the paper. The watercolour sits high in the frame, fully inside it; the lower quarter is calm green wallpaper and shadow. No text, no lettering, no watermark, no logo.
